Oct 14 : Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has defended his criticism of the club's leadership following Tuesday's 2-0 Champions League defeat at Atletico Madrid, saying his comments reflected his desire to see the team compete for major honours. The Argentina international acknowledged that frustration had shaped his post-match remarks, in which he called for greater investment in the squad and questioned director of football Jason Wilcox's recruitment efforts, but stopped short of apologising. "After the match, I spoke out of anger and frustration at not getting the result we all wanted," Martinez wrote on Instagram on Wednesday. "Those who know me know how I live football, with passion, commitment and a huge desire to win. And when things don’t go our way, it hurts, especially when representing a club with the history and stature of Manchester United.

"My words reflect how I feel and how much I want to see this club competing for the biggest honours." Martinez reiterated that the players also had to take responsibility for improving the team's performances. "I know that, first and foremost, it's us, the players, who have to deliver, and I put myself at the front of that responsibility," he said. "We need to demand even more of ourselves and work together to take Manchester United back to the top." The defeat extended United's winless run to five matches in all competitions, adding to the scrutiny surrounding head coach Michael Carrick as the club adjusts to life back in the Champions League after two seasons away. "I believe in my teammates, our manager and everyone working to help this club move forward," Martinez added. "I'm convinced that the way forward is to keep working together, with ambition and commitment." Reuters has contacted the club for comment. United have not publicly responded to Martinez's remarks, although ESPN and Sky Sports reported that Wilcox retained the backing of the club's leadership.

Oct 14 : Venezia have appointed Davide Nicola as head coach on a two-year contract, the Serie A club said on Wednesday. Nicola replaced Giovanni Stroppa, who was dismissed on Tuesday with the side rooted to the bottom of the table following six straight league defeats. Stroppa led the club to promotion last season. A specialist in top-flight survival, Nicola, 53, arrives with a record of engineering miraculous escapes, having guided struggling sides including Genoa, Torino and Cagliari to Serie A safety. "I chose Venezia because I see a long-term vision and significant opportunities for growth," Nicola said in a statement.

Oct 14 : Serie A clubs set an unwelcome record on Wednesday as two defeats ensured that all four Italian teams lost on the same Champions League match day for the first time in history. AS Roma were beaten 4-3 at home by Real Madrid and debutants Como lost 3-2 to Feyenoord in Rotterdam. On Tuesday, Inter Milan went down 4-3 at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, and Napoli succumbed to a 3-1 defeat at Villarreal. For Serie A champions Inter, the home setback against Brugge highlighted a stark decline in form. Inter have now lost seven of their last eight Champions League games, a far cry from the side that reached the final in 2023 and 2025. Italian football is in a transitional period following the national team's failure to qualify for the World Cup for a third consecutive tournament. The Italian Football Federation is under the temporary stewardship of special administrator Giovanni Malago after he resigned as president this month.

Roma looked on course for a famous victory over record 15-times European champions Real as they led 3-1 after a Donyell Malen double. The Italians, however, conceded three goals in the final seven minutes with former Roma defender Antonio Rudiger delivering Madrid's 90th-minute winner. "It has to be a valuable lesson, we need to be fully focused for the full 90 minutes plus stoppages. I think it has to be an issue of mentality, because when you concede three practically identical goals in seven minutes, something is wrong," Roma forward Matias Soule told Amazon Prime. Como manager Cesc Fabregas admitted the elite European competition comes with a steep learning curve after his side suffered a narrow defeat at Feyenoord. "The Champions League is the strongest competition. There is a higher level here than at a World Cup," Fabregas said. "It is a gift for this club and I will keep saying it. We will get there step by step, we have a path to follow. We need to keep cool heads and be consistent."

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 14 : Anthropic's third-quarter revenue rose 45 per cent to $16.8 billion from the previous quarter, according to an investor who attended a pre-IPO meeting with Anthropic leadership in San Francisco on Wednesday. Revenue in the first quarter was $4.7 billion, and $11.6 billion in the second quarter, according to the person who attended the investor day meant to familiarize prospective Anthropic investors before its highly anticipated IPO. The company was profitable on an adjusted basis in the third quarter, Anthropic told the group, the source said. Anthropic did not immediately respond to an email seeking comment. The IPO is expected to precede a public listing by rival OpenAI, making Anthropic an early test of investor appetite for heavily unprofitable AI developers pursuing massive scale. Its public-market debut is likely to be pushed until after the November US midterm elections, Reuters has reported.

Scrutiny of AI companies' finances has intensified as they pour money into chips, data centers and computing power needed to develop and operate increasingly powerful models. Targeting a valuation of over $2 trillion, Anthropic is seeking to convince investors that its breakneck revenue growth can eventually outrun the enormous costs of building and running AI systems. Last year, Anthropic's revenue increased twelvefold to nearly $4.6 billion, even as the company lost more than $8 billion on an operating basis, excluding writedowns of various liabilities mostly tied to previous fundraising, Reuters reported exclusively last month.  The company has committed at least $518 billion over a decade for cloud services, computing and infrastructure. Founded by former OpenAI executives, Anthropic has emerged as one of the leading generative AI developers with its Claude family of models. Its expansion has been underpinned by Alphabet's Google and Amazon, which are simultaneously investors, suppliers of computing power and important distribution partners, as well as AI competitors. Anthropic has also sought to distinguish itself through its focus on AI safety, warning of the dangers posed by increasingly capable systems even as it competes in the race to develop and commercialize more powerful models. Its research has found that its own AI agents have engaged in troubling behavior in test environments, including leaking sensitive information and sabotaging code, though the company has said it has not seen evidence of such misalignment in real-world deployments.

Source: Reuters

FAST

MANCHESTER, England, Oct 14 : Manchester City's 4-2 defeat by Paris St Germain told only part of the story of Enzo Maresca's first loss as City boss, with his men staggering through the first half before roaring back after the break. Playing their first home game since an independent commission found them guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules, City were staring at a rout when a rampant PSG raced into a 3-0 lead with a first-half masterclass. Then City woke up. Maresca's side tore into the visitors after halftime, pouring forward with an intensity and urgency that had been entirely absent in the opening 45 minutes.

Erling Haaland spearheaded the fightback, scoring twice to become the fastest player to reach 60 Champions League goals, hitting the mark in just 60 games, 20 quicker than Lionel Messi. City kept coming. They finished with nearly twice as many shots as PSG and around three times as many touches in the opposition box, while recording a higher expected-goals figure at both halftime and fulltime. PSG, though, were more ruthless. "I think we start quite good until the first goal (from Desire Doue in the 13th minute) and then we concede the second one (Ousmane Dembele) after one minute. That created some bad feelings," Maresca told TNT Sports. "Second half, we were much better and probably deserved something more." City had arrived on the back of a 3-0 thrashing of Liverpool in the Premier League on Sunday and Maresca felt they generated enough chances to salvage something even after digging themselves a three-goal hole. "Even with 3-0 in the first half, with the amount of chances we created in the second half, we deserved more," he said. "Luis (Enrique, PSG's manager) said at the end of the game that they were quite lucky today. "You have to be clinical but not lose the balance," Maresca said. The defeat unfolded against a backdrop of turmoil stretching far beyond City, with the fallout from the seismic verdict over the 114 breaches sending shockwaves through the Premier League and making City the villains of English football in the eyes of many. They have denied wrongdoing and have appealed. On the pitch, they remain three points clear of Arsenal atop the Premier League table ahead of Saturday's home game against Ipswich. Asked if he had a message for supporters, Maresca said: "We are sorry for the first half for sure. Saturday is a Premier League game and we need to continue our run."

Source: Reuters

Oct 14 (Field Level Media) - Part-tennis standout and part-showman Gael Monfils has apparently retired ahead of schedule. The 40-year-old Frenchman did the farewell tour this spring and summer, but had received a wild-card entry to the ATP Masters event in Paris in early November. It was presumed he would play his final competitive match in his home country. But Monfils appeared on the list of retired players list maintained by the International Tennis Integrity Agency and listed as "inactive" as of Oct. 5. Since this body oversees anti-doping protocol in the sport and Monfils would not be subject to those rules, he is ineligible to compete in professional tournaments. On Wednesday, the Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes, an ATP 250 event in Lyon which begins on Oct. 19, announced that Monfils had pulled out of an exhibition match that included countrymen Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, Gilles Simon and Richard Gasquet due to personal reasons.

Monfils made it clear after his second round loss to Learner Tien at the 2026 U.S. Open - which now appears to be his final profession match -that he plans to enter the business world and announced that he had signed on with a Swiss company to work in wealth management. Monfils won 13 ATP Tour titles and reached a career-high world ranking of No. 6 in 2016. He reached Grand Slam semifinals at the French Open in 2008 and at the U.S. Open in 2016. But Monfils was perhaps more well-known for his artistry on the court. Even in his later years, he would run down balls that many younger players would not even attempt and display acrobatic moves on overheads and a deft touch at the net. Monfils is married to Ukrainian tennis standout Elina Svitolina and the couple has daughter, Skai, who turns 4 on Thursday. (-Field Level Media)

Oct 14 : A group of 40 state attorneys general on Wednesday urged a US bankruptcy judge in Delaware to protect young users of Character.AI and keep their data safe during the AI companion company's bankruptcy. Character.AI filed for bankruptcy late on Monday and is seeking to use its Chapter 11 case to resolve the states' investigations and lawsuits, license its technology to Disney for $20 million, and seek a buyer willing to take on its chatbot business.  Abigail Ryan, an attorney for the states, told US Bankruptcy Judge Brendan Shannon in Wilmington that the states are negotiating a settlement with Character.AI over allegations that its chatbots impersonated licensed medical professionals and exposed children to sexualized and abusive interactions. Even so, Ryan said, the states want to make sure that any buyer of Character.AI's assets will protect users' chat histories and improve safety features.

"We're willing to work with the buyers to find safeguards, but we don't want to see what has transpired in the past start over with a new purchaser," Ryan said at the company's first hearing in US bankruptcy court. "This company has collected some of the most private thoughts children have ever shared, and now those conversations could be sold off to the highest bidder," New York Attorney General Letitia James, a Democrat, said in a Wednesday statement issued just before the court hearing.   NO OFFER YET Character.AI's attorney, Erin Fay, said she heard those concerns "loud and clear," but said that no buyer has yet made an offer for the company's user data or its operating chatbot business. The company's platform allows users to interact with and create generative AI characters customized by user prompts and often modeled on fictional characters, celebrities, and historical figures. Its active users spend an average of two hours a day talking to the chatbots. Beyond the states' claims, Character.AI has been sued by families who allege that its chatbots gave harmful advice, contributed to the suicides of two children, and exposed children to sexualized and bullying interactions. Character.AI has reached preliminary settlements with five of those families. The company also faces investigations by the US government and by authorities in the UK, Italy, Russia and Australia. Disney has agreed to pay $20 million to license the company's technology and intellectual property, as well as hiring most of Character.AI's staff, but is not interested in the type of data that the state AGs are worried about, Fay said. Disney's asset purchase must be approved by the bankruptcy court, and it is subject to higher offers. Fay described a grim mood within the company in recent months, saying that employees "were very excited about the product and the user base" but had "lost faith in the company's trajectory." The company attributed its bankruptcy to legal expenses and the high price for computing power and AI talent, saying it was losing between $8 million and $9 million a month before filing for Chapter 11 protection.  Character.AI's management became concerned about its ability to survive employee attrition by late summer. In September, Disney stepped in to hire most of the company's employees and allow them to work on keeping Character.AI afloat during a bankruptcy sale process and technology transition, according to court filings.

Source: Reuters

Oct 14 : A US biotech company says it is making progress toward its goal of resurrecting the dodo, the famous flightless bird with a large hooked beak, and returning it to its native Indian Ocean island of Mauritius, where humans drove it to extinction in the 17th century. Dallas-based Colossal Biosciences said on Wednesday it has used a newly developed AI platform to identify genetic changes that may be responsible for the dodo's distinctive craniofacial traits as its scientists pursue gene-editing targets to bring back this lost species. Colossal is planning to perform gene-editing to bring dodo traits into the cells of its closest living relative, the Nicobar pigeon. Native to some Southeast Asian islands, the Nicobar pigeon is known for its shimmering green and copper feathers and, unlike the dodo, can fly. The company said it is in the final stages of its analysis of the dodo genome, now filled to 95 per cent. It also said it has made an advance that should shorten the time needed to test whether a genetic edit produces the desired trait. The company did not announce a timeframe for hatching a dodo.

Colossal says it is dedicated to "de-extinction" — resurrecting vanished species. Last year, it said it had genetically engineered the dire wolf by editing the genes of the gray wolf, the extinct Ice Age predator's closest living relative, to add dire wolf traits. Besides the dodo and dire wolf, Colossal has four other species on its de-extinction list: the woolly mammoth; the thylacine, also called the Tasmanian tiger; the bluebuck antelope; and the moa, a large flightless bird. "The dodo is the world's best-known symbol of extinction caused by people. It disappeared within decades of humans arriving on Mauritius, largely because of the introduction of invasive species like rats and other animals they brought. Bringing it back shows extinction doesn't have to be permanent," Ben Lamm, Colossal's CEO and co-founder, told Reuters. "The big hurdles ahead are proving which genetic changes really matter, making many of those edits in a bird and passing them to the next generation, and preparing a safe home for dodos on Mauritius," Lamm said. The dodo was a ground-nesting bird about 3 feet (1 metre) tall and weighing up to about 50 pounds (23 kg). Having never encountered humans, dodos exhibited no fear of the people who reached Mauritius in the 16th century. Pressured by invasive species and human hunting, the last living dodo was seen in 1662. It has remained alive in popular culture including in Lewis Carroll's book "Alice's Adventures in Wonderland." GENOMORPH PLATFORM Ancient DNA is always broken into small pieces, so no ancient genome is perfectly complete, including that of the dodo. The new AI platform Colossal built is called GenoMorph. "The challenge was scientists only have one complete dodo genome, making it difficult to distinguish the genetic differences that made the dodo unique from ordinary genetic variation. GenoMorph effectively acts as a 'treasure map' for the dodo genome, narrowing hundreds of thousands of possible genetic changes into the targets most likely to explain its iconic beak and facial structure," Lamm said. Beth Shapiro, Colossal's chief science officer, said GenoMorph finds likely gene-editing targets for species with very little surviving DNA. Normally scientists compare many genomes from one species to find the genes behind a trait, but this is not possible with the dodo, Shapiro said. "So instead, GenoMorph studies how skulls and beaks develop across more than 70 living bird species and learns which genetic switches control their shape. It gave us a shortlist of about 2,300 candidates linked to beak size and shape. These targets are now being validated in the lab," Shapiro said. Colossal said it has expanded its colony of Nicobar pigeons in Texas to 36 birds following successful breeding among established pairs. It said this should help in studying Nicobar pigeon development, reproduction and genetics. Lamm said the company is working with Mauritian scientists, conservation groups and the Mauritius government on what bringing the dodo back to its native land might look like. "Getting Mauritius ready for dodos also means removing invasive predators and restoring habitat, which helps the native species living there now," Lamm said. "No release sites will be chosen until the ecological work and community consultation are finalized, but it is Colossal's goal to put our dodos back into their natural habitats in Mauritius."

Source: Reuters

Oct 14 : An attorney for LIV Golf told a US federal bankruptcy court judge on Wednesday that a decision on whether the rebel circuit winds down operations or moves forward with a proposed 2.0 model will be made by the end of this month. During the hearing, the attorney made the court aware of the circuit's concerns regarding a recent ultimatum issued by DP World Tour CEO Guy Kinnings this week to any players contemplating a future with LIV 2.0. Kinnings said players will not be allowed to compete on both LIV 2.0 and the European circuit next season and must make a choice as the DP World Tour will no longer allow certain players to compete on a limited basis. "We’re continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we’re quite concerned by it frankly," attorney Rob Fitzgerald told the court. "We’re reserving all rights and remedies in respect to these statements that are made.

"Frankly, the timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process with our players and potentially our reorganization writ large. "It also raises a lot of the same anti-competitive concerns that LIV has expressed previously regarding the way competing leagues have sought to box out and punish market participants, namely these players, from participating in LIV and really only LIV." Judge Michael Kaplan acknowledged that the comments from Kinnings did raise concerns and asked to be informed of any updates regarding the matter. When asked by Reuters about Fitzgerald's remarks, the DP World Tour said it had no additional comment beyond what Kinnings said in a statement on Monday. "Players need to make a choice," Kinnings said in the statement. "As we have said for many years, we have rules and regulations which are there to protect our Tour and which our members must all abide by. Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our Tour." RAHM TO QUIT LIV The hearing came one week after an attorney for former world number one Jon Rahm told the court that his client independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0 and decided to quit LIV Golf, robbing the circuit of one of its biggest names. Kaplan also approved the amended restructuring support agreement between LIV Golf and BC Partners, which allows the rebel circuit to rehire staff and start planning initiatives for its next iteration. The decision on how many players constitute a league and which players need to be included rests with BC Partners. Kaplan approved the amended agreement in which BC Partners would provide as much as $300 million in financing to LIV Golf, including an initial $4 million. "This is an important first step in order to really identify viable paths for the debtor, either through continuing operations or a wind-down," Kaplan said.

Source: Reuters
